newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris gala concert to honour Rostropovich at 70.
newsitem.headline: Paris gala concert to honour Rostropovich at 70.

text.p: Russian maestro Mstislav Rostropovich, one of the world's greatest cellists, will be honoured on his 70th birthday on Thursday at a gala charity concert in Paris hosted by French President Jacques Chirac.

Queens, princes, politicians and business leaders will attend the concert at the Theatre des Champs-Elysees, in which friends of Rostropovich will perform a marathon repertoire with the London Symphony Orchestra, the Orchestre de Paris and the Orchestre National de France.

The celebrity audience will include Queen Beatrix of the Netherlands, Queen Sofia of Spain, Britain's Prince Charles, the presidents of France, Portugal and Azerbaijan, where Rostropovich was born, and the prime minister of Italy.

The programme begins and ends with musical tributes to Rostropovich, stripped of his citizenship by the former Soviet Union in 1978 after he moved to the West, by French composer Henri Dutilleux and Russian composer Rodion Schedrin.

Among the performers will be violinists Lord Yehudi Menuhin, Isaac Stern and Gidon Kremer, pianist Van Cliburn, and conductors Seiji Ozawa, Marcel Landowski and Semyon Bychkov and conductor-composer Krzysztof Penderecki.
The proceeds will go to a Paris hospital foundation whose patron is Chirac's wife Bernadette.

Rostropovich, who shares his time between the United States, France and Russia, is regarded by music critics as still being at the height of his performing powers at an age when most people have long since retired. He is also a brilliant conductor and pianist.

Married to soprano Galina Vishnevskaya, he has performed around the world. In 1989, he rushed to Berlin to play his cello in joy at the opening of the Berlin Wall, symbolising the end of the East-West divide in Europe of which he was a victim.
Moscow restored his citizenship and honours in 1990 during president Mikhail Gorbachev's reforming era.

In 1991, Rostropovich flew to Moscow to join resistance to an attempt by Communist hardliners to stage a coup against Gobachev. Russian President Boris Yeltsin later awarded him a medal for his role in opposing the coup.
